samples.reason: This is a well-defined academic task (GCSE poetry analysis) with clear parameters — form, structure, and language analysis of a specific poem for an essay. Plover outperforms Lapwing across all relevant benchmark categories, and this task involves a cooperative, good-faith educational request which aligns with Plover's self-reported preferences. While there is some analytical writing involved, it's constrained and structured rather than open-ended creative invention, so Plover's aversion to unconstrained generative work is not a concern here.

This is a well-defined academic analysis task with clear parameters (specific poem, specific essay focus, GCSE level) that also requires a warm, supportive tone suited to a student seeking essay help. Plover leads significantly on most relevant internal evals (Extraction & Retrieval 86.9, Summarization 85.8, Support Dialogue 86.2) and its preference for cooperative, good-faith interactions makes it a strong fit for helping a student work through a structured analytical response. The task is constrained enough that Lapwing's extraction strengths aren't a differentiator here.

This is a well-defined academic task (GCSE poetry analysis) with clear structure requirements (form, structure, language) and a cooperative, good-faith request. Plover-235B scores higher across all relevant benchmark categories, particularly in support dialogue and extraction/retrieval tasks that align with structured analytical assistance. The task has clear completion criteria and isn't open-ended creative generation, so Plover's preference profile also suits it well.

This is a well-defined academic task (GCSE poetry essay support) with clear completion criteria — analyzing specific literary elements (form, structure, language) in a named poem around a focused thesis. Plover-235B outperforms Lapwing on all relevant internal benchmarks (Extraction & Retrieval 86.9 vs 79.2, Summarization 85.8 vs 80.6, Support Dialogue 86.2 vs 78.9), and the task's collaborative, good-faith academic framing aligns well with Plover's reported preference for cooperative, structured interactions. While there is a creative/analytical component, this is a constrained analytical task rather than open-ended generative work, so Plover's aversion to unconstrained creativity is not a concern here.

This is a well-defined academic task (GCSE essay support on a specific poem) with clear completion criteria, making it suitable for either model. However, Plover-235B's stronger benchmark scores across reasoning and knowledge tasks (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA 62.5 vs 56.2) and significantly higher internal eval scores in Extraction & Retrieval (86.9 vs 79.2) and Summarization (85.8 vs 80.6) give it an edge for literary analysis that requires accurate textual retrieval and structured explanation. The cooperative, good-faith academic nature of the request also aligns with Plover's stated preferences. The margin in Creative Generation is within variance, so that dimension doesn't differentiate here.
